text:
maria: heads up - after yesterday's canary we see a 15-25% p95 decode latency increase on host-side for short-chat workloads. datadog flame points at grpc write path + tokenization hotspots.

sanjay: saw the same. quick flame snapshot: host -> parse_token -> proto_unmarshal -> writev. KV cache hit rate dropped ~8% during ramp. attaching sample traces (will paste snippets).

kelly: can you paste the flame snippet and the exact config flip? any kernel selection changes in that canary?

sanjay: flame snippet: `parse_token` dominated user CPU, lots of time in `proto_unmarshal`. The canary enabled a kernel-hint change (prefer avx512 for decoder kernels) and we added a pre-unpack proto stage in host preproc. I think the pre-unpack is the noisy one.

maria: numbers: baseline p95 (short-chat) = 45ms -> canary = 56ms. Host CPU user went 18% -> 26% at same QPS. grpc active thread count +30%.

raj: quick repro: spin a tiny load (N=200 qps short-chat). toggle envs: `PREUNPACK=0` reduces p95 by ~9%. Toggling `GRPC_WRITEV=0` (disable writev) also helps small bursts.

nate: note: small write coalescing change in the canary made frames flush earlier which increases syscall count. Might explain writev path surge. We should consider a 1ms coalesce timer instead of immediate flush.

perf-bot: benchmark-run summary:
- short-chat-128: baseline_p95=45ms
- canary_p95=56ms
- preunpack_off_p95=51ms
- writev_off_p95=49ms
(artifacts: flameshots/url)

kelly: KV cache behavior: evictions spike during canary. We changed the admission policy to favor large-seq entries; that pushed out small-chat keys. Hit rate down ~=8pp for short keys.

sanjay: hypothesis: pre-unpack increases parse CPU, delaying finishing of request handling and increasing time between token generation and kv touch -> transiently hurting locality and causing more evictions.

maria: agreed. proposed immediate mitigation: revert pre-unpack change; re-enable writev coalescing with a small timer; revert KV admission to size-first for short keys. Also add a quick microbench for tokenization path.

raj: plan to run a canary with `PREUNPACK=0`, `WRITEV_COALESCE_MS=1`, `KV_ADMIT_MODE=small-first`. Kicking off on canary-3 now, will collect p95/kv metrics and flame.

raj: (20m later) quick results: p95 back to 47ms, KV hit restored +6pp, host CPU user down 5%. grpc write spikes largely reduced. Looks promising.

maria: awesome. roll back the pre-unpack change and hold off on AVX512 kernel hint rollout for short-sequence profiles until we have a targeted perf test.

kelly: follow-ups: 1) add proto-parse microbench to CI that exercises 1-16 token requests, 2) add a perf alert: KV hit drop >4pp sustained for 10m, 3) add kernel-selection unit test to simulate short seq distribution and prevent AVX512 path being chosen incorrectly. I'll open PRs and link here.

nate: small note: we should also add a benchmark that measures syscall/writev rate per request for tiny responses to catch coalescing regressions early.

maria: +1 to all. Good triage. Assign owners: @kelly tests/alerts, @raj canary runs + rollback, @sanjay follow up on proto unpack micro-optim. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(attachments: flameshot-1.png, kv-evictions.csv, perf-bot-run-1754443260)
